clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock moved from 7:43 p.m. at the close of Week 41 to 7:42 p.m. by the end of Week 42, a shift of roughly a third of a minute. This small movement reflects a week in which severe executive pressure was met by unusually forceful institutional and electoral resistance, producing rough balance rather than a clear advance in either direction.

grand_total_points.note: Net movement was slightly negative, reflecting rough balance between severe executive pressure and unusually forceful judicial and electoral resistance.

delta_summary.moral_floor: Breaches touched all six baseline traits this week, most severely restraint and good faith, but institutional resistance was unusually substantial, including permanent injunctions, sustained SNAP enforcement, and a sitting judge's resignation in protest.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: The floor did not rise this week, and it did not fall further either. It was fought over in full public view, with real costs already landing on real people before the contest was resolved.

traits_moved.note: Twenty-four traits registered measurable movement this week, an unusually high number reflecting the density of confrontation across nearly every democratic domain.

long_synopsis: Week 42 concentrated an unusual density of confrontation into seven days. SNAP benefits lapsed for the first time in sixty-one years, and the administration resisted a court order to fund them, with the vice president calling the ruling absurd before the Supreme Court paused relief. The Justice Department indicted Comey, James, and Bolton within days of a presidential demand, while a federal magistrate rebuked the process and a Reagan-appointed judge resigned in protest. Decisive Democratic wins in Virginia, New Jersey, New York City, and California's redistricting vote met fraud claims, election monitors, and a Fourteenth Amendment gambit against New York's mayor-elect. Courts blocked National Guard deployments in five cities and issued a permanent injunction in Portland, even as unilateral war-making abroad continued unchecked. A mass pardon of 2020 election-subversion figures closed the week. The clock moved barely at all, reflecting rough balance between severe pressure and real resistance.
short_synopsis: Food aid, prosecutions, and war powers were used as executive leverage this week, while courts blocked troop deployments, voters delivered decisive results, and a federal judge resigned in protest of weaponized law. The clock barely moved, reflecting a week fought to a standstill.
